content.text: I have what I need. Section 14.3, together with §11.1.1.4 and §10.3, provides the transition and data-return package.

input.quote: transfer control to PB of any or all Clinical Trials being conducted by or on behalf of SFJ or its Affiliate as of the effective date of termination and (y) continue to conduct such Clinical Trials being conducted by or on behalf of SFJ or an Affiliate as of the effective date of termination for up to [***] to enable such transfer to be completed without interruption of any such Clinical Trial
input.rationale: The Agreement contains a usable post-termination transition and data-return regime running in our favour, so no insert is needed. Section 14.3 (surviving termination per §14.4.3.2) obliges SFJ on any termination to: (i) assign sole and exclusive ownership of the Trial Data Package and Research Results to PB (§14.3.1); (ii) assign all Product Filings and, where not immediately transferable, give PB the benefit of them plus "such assistance and cooperation as necessary or reasonably requested by PB" (§14.3.2); (iii) deliver true, correct and complete copies of all Product Filings and disclose all previously-undisclosed Research Results within a set period after assignment (§14.3.3); (iv) at PB's sole election, either wind down the Clinical Trials at SFJ's cost or transfer control to PB and continue conducting them for a defined transition period so the transfer occurs without interruption (§14.3.4); and (v) assign all Clinical Trial, CRO and Vendor Agreements and cooperate on notices to Sites, Investigators and CROs (§14.3.5). Section 11.1.1.4 independently vests sole and exclusive ownership of the Trial Data Package in PB upon termination "in accordance with any termination clause or section of this Agreement," and PB holds/jointly maintains the Clinical Trials Database and Master File (§§3.5.3, 3.5.4), so our data is not stranded with SFJ. Section 10.3 handles the deletion leg: on expiry or termination, Confidential Information is returned or destroyed at the Disclosing Party's direction, "with such destruction being certified in writing by an authorized officer of the Receiving Party," subject to sensible survival and one-archival-copy carve-outs. This meets the preferred position (transition assistance, data return, certified deletion) and is not walk-away territory — there is no immediate-deletion or no-return risk. Two points noted but not flagged: the transition and delivery periods are redacted ([***]), so we cannot confirm they match the 6-month/30-day benchmarks, and the transition-assistance leg of §14.3.4(ii) is at PB's cost and expense rather than at then-current rates, which is the customary allocation here given SFJ elects nothing. Section 14.3 applies only if SFJ has not triggered a Program Transfer under §3.20; that alternative path is a separately negotiated funding remedy governed by the Exhibit O Program Transfer Agreement and belongs to the change-of-control/remedies rules rather than this one.
